newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Rugby sees fruits of shake-up in 1997.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Rugby sees fruits of shake-up in 1997.

text.p: Britain's Rugby Group Plc warned of more job cuts ahead on Thursday as its shake-up continued, but said the fruits should begin to feed through in 1997 after reporting a fall in 1996 underlying profit.

The building materials group announced pretax profits of 52.6 million pounds ($84.3 million) compared with 45.8 million, after a 9.9 million exceptional charge in 1996 against a 26.9 million charge in 1995.
But underlying operating profits fell 12 percent to 64.6 million.
Rugby froze its year dividend at 3.6 pence per share and turnover barely changed at 1.144 billion pounds.
Peter Johnson, group chief executive, said 1997 would see further job cuts on top of those already announced but added that its restructuring efforts would bear fruit in the 1997 figures.
"The actions we have taken in 1996 will re-establish Rugby's position as a leading performer in its sector without depending on improvements in our markets," he said.
The Australian market is not seen rebounding until later this year and will be weaker than in past cycles. European markets will remain tough and the U.S. is not expected to match its 1996 levels.

He later told Reuters that the shake-up was not over. "There could be further rationalisation of jobs," he said. Some 535 job cuts had already been announced, but after some job creation, the net cut was 370 jobs to date.
Rugby said the benefits from cost cutting and changes at its John Carr, Rugby Building Products (RBP) and Stegbar units would be felt in 1997.
"We expect some of the results of restructuring to come through in 1997, with substantial progress being made next year," said the chief executive.
Volumes to date are ahead, with British cement up by "not
far off 10 percent" in the first 10 weeks, he told Reuters. In joinery, volume growth exceeds that level, but he warned both were compared with a very low base in 1996.
Looking at a divisional breakdown of the 1996 figures, cement and lime saw turnover rise to 195.5 million pounds from 190.7 million, with profits down to 31.9 million from 34.2 million.
Joinery saw total sales of 314.9 million versus 336 million, with profits down to 19.4 million from 25.6 million.
Manufacturing and distribution in the U.S. saw sales of 460.1 million versus 446.3 million, with profits up to 11.9 million from 10.2 million.
Metal Building Products rose to 174.1 million from 170.1 million, with profits slipping to 5.8 million from 7.1 million. ($ = 0.624 British Pounds)
